newsitem.title: UK: Brazil warns Europe against barring its products.
newsitem.headline: Brazil warns Europe against barring its products.

text.p: Brazil, facing a record trade deficit, on Monday urged the European Union to drop barriers to its products, telling member countries to abide by international trade rules.
"Brazilian agricultural exports still face barriers to entry in the European market," President Fernando Henrique Cardoso told a conference.

"Many of these exports compete with similar ones produced within the European Union with the benefit of high subsidies which create artificial conditions for competition and do away with the comparative advantages of our products."
Trade has become a growing issue in Brazil. Last year's record trade deficit of $5.6 billion is expected to balloon to more than $8.0 billion this year.
Cardoso said it was important that EU countries stuck to commitments agreed in international trade negotiations.
"We must strive to avoid that Brazil and the other member states of (the Latin American trade group) Mercosul be eventually confined to an unfavourable postion in their relations with Europe.
"That would be a tremendous setback for countries such as ours which have taken truly revolutionary steps to open their economies to foreign competition," he said.
